subject.title: macOS launchd Gateway still restarts via gateway-update/update.run; document and honor auto-update kill-switch

question: Should `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` suppress explicit Gateway control-plane `update.run` managed handoffs on supervised/headless installs, or should it remain limited to configured background `update.auto` applies?
rationale: The source fix is narrow, but the behavior changes an operator-requested update path and the public meaning of an existing environment kill-switch; automation should not choose that contract.

options.title: Extend the kill-switch to Gateway handoffs
options.body: Treat the env var as a supervised/headless package-update restart kill-switch, gate `update.run` handoff creation, and document the broader scope.

options.title: Keep the current narrower scope
options.body: Leave `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` limited to configured background auto-update applies and document that explicit `update.run` can still restart managed services.

options.title: Introduce a separate explicit update-run policy
options.body: Keep the existing env var stable and add a new maintainer-approved config or env policy for blocking explicit control-plane update restarts.

recommendation.title: Extend the kill-switch to Gateway handoffs
recommendation.body: Treat the env var as a supervised/headless package-update restart kill-switch, gate `update.run` handoff creation, and document the broader scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the kill-switch and recently worked on package service-state cutover, making them the best available owner for the scope decision.
